provide valuable information for diagnosing faults and conducting security analysis in software-intensive systems. Although log sequence anomaly detection has garnered increasing attention and achieved satisfactory performance, it remains a challenging task due to several inherent issues, including continuously evolving event templates and noisy data introduced during log generation and processing. To address these challenges, we propose ATCC, a novel enhancement approach for log anomaly detection that combines adversarial fine-tuning and contrastive learning. The base model is first trained with its original objective function until it stabilizes. During the adversarial fine-tuning stage, a tailored objective function integrating classification loss, contrastive loss, and consistency loss is employed to improve model robustness. Specifically, this stage enhances both detection robustness and explanation robustness. We evaluate ATCC by using it to enhance three representative supervised anomaly detection models across three widely used benchmark datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our method improves both detection robustness and explanation robustness of existing log anomaly detection models against evolving and noisy logs while maintaining comparable
